section_summary.extract_value: This section presents the estimation results for a study with a sample size of 400 salespeople. It details the influence of previous technology use and goal orientations (Performance Orientation - PO, and Learning Orientation - LO) on sales performance trajectories over time, including linear, quadratic, and cubic trends. The results support hypotheses regarding the anticipated performance trajectory and the differential effects of LO and PO on performance decline, recovery, and plateau phases.

section_summary.extract_value: This section presents the estimation results from a hierarchical linear model, detailing how covariates (openness to change, experience, previous technology use) and goal orientations (Learning Orientation and Performance Orientation) influence sales performance trajectories over time. It discusses the significant effects of these predictors on the linear, quadratic, and cubic trends of performance, supporting several hypotheses (H1a-H1c, H2a-H2c, H3a-H3c). Numerical simulations and plots are also described to illustrate the impact of goal orientations on performance plateaus.

Asset Caption.extract_value: B: Estimation Results Notes: Y = sales performance per quota, OC = openness to change, EXP = experience, and USE = previous technology use. Cells depict unstandardized parameter estimates, and values in parentheses are standard errors. i = individual, n = 400, t = 0, ..., 11. For the unrestricted model, the between-subjects variation is incorporated in the Level 1 error structure (Raudenbush et al. 2001).
